feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with a clear senior digital communications profile and logical career progression within one organization. It reads professionally and shows solid scope, but impact would be stronger with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and skills sections align well with senior digital strategy, communications, and platform leadership roles.  
- Credible progression: promotions within NACo demonstrate growth, trust, and increasing responsibility over time.  
- Good specificity: strong tools/platform detail (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, etc.) adds credibility and supports the strategic claims.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include impact such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign outcomes.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating these would improve scannability.  
- Fix writing/style consistency: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; add the serial comma consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); standardize punctuation in bullets; “cross-channel” vs “Multi-channel” is a minor style inconsistency. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that reflect the candidate’s public-sector/advocacy niche.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” and lead with the current brand: “Digital communications and strategy leader…”
- Replace generic phrases like “expert in” with stronger, more concrete wording tied to this CV: web/CMS modernization, cross-channel operations, analytics, and governance.
- Add sector relevance: mention public-sector, membership, or mission-driven organizations to better match NACo experience.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, CMS modernization, digital governance, and the workflows and analytics that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflows and systems” overlaps with Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets; keep the intro high-level.
- Avoid adding tool names here, since technical platforms are already covered elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper phrasing and pluralize where appropriate: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Consider replacing “Web & CMS administration” with “Web platform & CMS management” for a more senior tone.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” is slightly abstract; “Systems architecture & process design” or “Content operations & workflow design” may read more clearly.
- Keep this section high-level and let Topline Skills/Technical + IT carry the tools and platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination,” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat language already covered in the header and Soft Skills.
- Analytics, workflow, multimedia, and web/CMS themes also recur in Topline Skills, so avoid expanding this block further.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around highest-value outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets, e.g.:
- “Built and optimized cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Provided hands-on CMS/front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, time saved, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “Drupal/web improvement” repeat heavily from the 2022–2024 NACo role; frame this entry as post-staff consulting leadership and new initiatives.
- The microsite and AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; keep the CV item higher-level if those projects stay detailed elsewhere.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope-and-impact line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and organization-wide communications operations.”
- Combine the website bullets and foreground outcome: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more results-based: add email/social performance if available (growth, engagement, CTR, list size, campaign output) instead of “reaching tens of thousands.”
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, events and recurring video content”; “Expanded analytics stack… to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-program growth also appears in earlier roles; focus here on building the studio and scaling organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Tighten it around what was uniquely expanded here: recurring newsletter operations, advocacy video, and cross-team editorial coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + distinct contribution: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and publishing consistency.
- If possible, add outcomes: email open/click rates, video views, production volume, turnaround time, or stakeholder adoption.
- Replace weak phrasing like “helped improve” and “helping scale” with direct ownership verbs: “improved,” “standardized,” “expanded,” “established.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” duplicates the Director role; keep this version more execution- and systems-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the prior role; frame this entry as formalizing/scaling the program, not starting it.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modernize/clarify the tooling.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & Technical Implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; if kept, place last or label as legacy support.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: **Front-end:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript | **Integrations & tagging:** APIs, Google Tag Manager | **Edge/DevOps:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If space allows elsewhere, tie tools to outcomes in recent roles (e.g., “used for CMS enhancements, tagging deployment, workflow automation, and edge-based web improvements”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Technical Implementation” may also overlap with automation/workflow items if GitHub Actions is described elsewhere.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and grouped to signal actual operating strength.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and trim lower-value collaboration tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Put the strongest, most relevant systems first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If accurate, add a light proficiency cue in the heading or formatting, e.g. “Automation & Workflow Systems: Airtable (system design), Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana…”
- Consider dropping Slack/Teams entirely if space is tight; they are expected and don’t add much differentiation for a senior digital leader.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals—listing all four may feel padded unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise-scale email/engagement capability and aligning the wording with the CV’s public-sector communications focus.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/context rather than more tools: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and member communications**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies and repeated email references across multiple NACo roles; avoid adding generic phrases like “email strategy” here unless tied to platform capability

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer

items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. items.aiFeedback:

- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped onboard and guide…”

- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching or piloting the format.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version lighter and more execution-oriented.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator

- Consider a stronger action/result version: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, creating a new multimedia channel for member and policy communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in later digital roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general communications support; later entries already establish that progression.
